bullets.title: NVDA: Citi reiterates Buy/$300 PT; China H200 approval lifts stock +3.7%
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on NVDA with $300 PT (~47% upside) based on ~28x P/E on CY27E EPS of ~$11.9; management confirmed full roadmap intact despite Kyber/Rubin delays, reiterated mid-70s gross margin guidance and 50% cash flow return target. Separately, China approved limited H200 chip purchases (<200k units) for top AI firms (Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek), a modest positive; Blackwell's 25x power efficiency vs. Hopper and expanding non-hyperscaler demand (sovereigns, enterprises, neoclouds) cited as structural tailwinds.

bullets.title: AVGO/AAPL: $30B+ multiyear chip deal through 2031; AVGO +4.8%, Citi Buy on both
bullets.body: Apple and Broadcom announced a $30B+ multiyear agreement through 2031 covering custom ASICs for Apple's AI infrastructure and wireless connectivity chips, producing 15B+ US-made chips and expanding AVGO's Colorado facility with $1.5B capex. Citi maintains Buy on both: AAPL PT $315 (33x CY2027 EPS), AVGO PT $500 (20x F28 EPS). Meaningful revenue ramp from Apple's custom AI silicon expected 2029/2030 as Apple's in-house LLM (currently ~2-3 years behind frontier models) matures.

bullets.title: AAPL/DELL: PC shipments fall 4.9% YoY in 2Q26 — first decline in 9 quarters
bullets.body: Citi notes worldwide PC units declined 4.9% YoY in 2Q26 to 68M units, ending nine consecutive quarters of growth, driven by exhausted pull-forward demand and memory/component shortages expected to persist until early 2028. IDC forecasts 2H26 unit declines of 19%; Citi estimates -15% for full 2026. AAPL gained share (9.9% from 9.3%), Dell slipped (13.6% from 15.2%); Citi maintains Buy on AAPL and DELL, Neutral on HPE.

bullets.title: RH: Upgraded to Neutral from Sell at Goldman; PT raised to $155 from $86
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs upgraded RH to Neutral from Sell, raising PT to $155 from $86, expecting a period of topline stability with potential acceleration into 2027. Separately, Citi's retail web traffic tracker showed RH became less positive vs. prior month in June Week 5.

bullets.title: SHOP: Q2 bar is 30% revenue growth; Q3 guide needs mid-to-high 20s to work
bullets.body: Analyst commentary indicates the stock requires 30% revenue growth in Q2 (guide: 30-31%) and at least mid-to-high 20s for Q3 revenue guidance to sustain performance. FCF margin expected at 16% in Q2 and 18% in Q3; mid-20% revenue decel in Q3 viewed as too aggressive even accounting for tougher comps. SHOP traded -4.0% in Canadian session.

bullets.title: FOXA: Down 2.8% as Netflix/Disney/YouTube weigh bids for 2030/2034 World Cup rights
bullets.body: Fox Corp fell 2.8% after reports that Netflix, Disney, and YouTube are considering bids for 2030 and 2034 FIFA World Cup broadcast rights, raising competitive pressure on Fox's sports rights franchise.

bullets.title: T: Wells Fargo initiates Underweight at $18 PT; VZ Equal Weight at $43
bullets.body: Wells Fargo initiated AT&T at Underweight with a $18 PT and Verizon at Equal Weight with a $43 PT. TMUS was initiated at Equal Weight ($170 PT) and fell 2.5% on a new executive appointment.

bullets.title: TTD: HSBC upgrades to Hold from Reduce, PT $20
bullets.body: HSBC upgraded The Trade Desk to Hold from Reduce with a $20 price target.

bullets.title: META: Secures 250MW long-term power deal with Capital Power for Alberta data center (H2 2028)
bullets.body: Meta entered a >10-year energy supply agreement for 250MW with Capital Power Corporation to support its Sturgeon County, Alberta data center anticipated to be in service H2 2028. Separately, Meta is testing AI glasses with continuous camera/audio recording capability.

bullets.title: GOOGL/AMZN: Scotiabank sees both as key AI capex beneficiaries; Outperform on each
bullets.body: Scotiabank argues market overweights near-term hyperscaler capex concerns and underweights control of scarce compute assets, with power emerging as the new bottleneck. AMZN rated Sector Outperform PT $325, GOOGL Sector Outperform PT $450, META Sector Perform PT $700.

bullets.title: BE: Down 5.7% after Hunterbrook Capital discloses short position
bullets.body: Bloom Energy fell 5.7% after Hunterbrook Media reported that Hunterbrook Capital has established a short position in the stock. The broader utilities sector also underperformed amid hawkish FOMC minutes signaling possible rate hikes.

bullets.title: MDB: KGI Securities initiates Outperform with $470 PT (32% upside)
bullets.body: KGI Securities initiated MongoDB at Outperform with a $470 price target, implying ~32% upside from the ~$356 current price. FactSet consensus average target is $399.82.

bullets.title: HF positioning: Systematic and fundamental managers aggressively cutting AI longs
bullets.body: Systematic long-short managers are down 3.6% since June 22 (worst drawdown since summer 2025), with YTD returns falling from 14.4% to 10.8%; fundamental L/S managers down 2.2% over same period but still up 15.5% YTD. Fundamental managers aggressively cutting AI/Info Tech long exposure that drove all YTD alpha through June 22; gross leverage pushed to bottom decile over the past year.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Data center REITs +31.6% in H1 2026; UBS warns valuation rerating largely complete
bullets.body: UBS notes US REITs returned +17.6% in H1 2026, with data centers the top sector at +31.6%. However, global real estate now trades at only a 2.5% discount to NAV vs. the 10-year average discount of 10.2%, and forward P/E has rerated to 16.7x in line with the 10-year average — future returns must come from earnings delivery rather than multiple expansion.

bullets.title: AFRM: Barclays initiates payments fintech coverage; PYPL underweight as branded checkout share collapses
bullets.body: Barclays initiated coverage across payments/fintech, flagging slowing secular growth and limited AI monetization progress. Key call: PYPL initiated Underweight as Branded Checkout share fell from 44% of Visa e-commerce transactions in 2019 to 16% in 2025. FISV also initiated at Equal Weight after president Dhivya Suryadevara resigned; stock fell 4.0%.

bullets.title: STX/WDC: Citi hosting storage supply-demand webcast; memory shortages seen persisting to early 2028
bullets.body: Citi hosted a storage supply-demand dynamics webcast featuring TRENDFOCUS analysts covering HDD/SSD and NAND Flash trends. Context: PC memory shortages cited across multiple notes as a primary driver of 2Q26 PC unit declines, with shortages expected to persist until early 2028.

bullets.title: VRT/industrials: MasTec acquires Superior Group for $1.65B targeting hyperscaler data center market
bullets.body: MasTec acquired The Superior Group for $1.65B (6.9x 2026 EBITDA) to expand its hyperscaler data center exposure. Industrials sector declined 106bps vs. S&P -28bps, with aerospace/defense down 2.4% and homebuilders down 4.1%.

bullets.title: SHOP/CRWV: Notable movers in Canadian session — CRWV +5.1%, SHOP -4.0%
bullets.body: In the Canadian mid-afternoon session, CoreWeave (CRWV) rose 5.1% and Shopify (SHOP) fell 4.0%. Celestica (CLS) gained 3.0% and SanDisk (SNDK) rose 3.1%.

bullets.title: Macro: FOMC minutes hawkish; near-term rate hike risk if core PCE stays above 3.3%
bullets.body: June FOMC minutes showed almost all participants would support tightening if inflation remains elevated, with price pressures becoming more broad-based. The base case per multiple analysts is a gradual shift toward rate hikes around year-end; median 3.3% core PCE aligns with no hikes or one hike, while 3.5% aligns with 2-3 hikes. Front-end rate volatility likely to remain elevated under Chair Warsh.
